description: 71 Specialized Skills for Full-Stack Developers. Transform Claude Code into your expert pair programmer.
readmeExcerpt:
--- ## What's New in v0.5.0 v0.5.0 rebuilds the project workflow around specs. Tickets stay in your tracker, specs live as Markdown in your repo, and each ticket is built with its failing test first, by hand or in an unattended goal run. **Install** - The plugin now ships from the `plugin/` folder on `main`, listed by the root marketplace entry. The [Quick Start](#quick-start) commands are unchanged. Updating the plugin installs what `main` holds, and the separate `plugin` distribution branch is gone. See [plugin/README.md](https://github.com/jeffallan/claude-skills/blob/main/plugin/README.md). - The workflow commands need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and a `.claude/workflow-config.json`, which a setup wizard offers to create. See [Tracker Setup](docs/TRACKER_SETUP.md). **Adopting an existing codebase** - `intake` documents the code, pins its current behavior in characterization tests and records each bug it finds as an `F-NNN` finding while leaving the behavior unchanged. It also writes a baseline spec and `docs/system-description.md`, and runs by hand or as one goal with a commit per item. See [Intake](docs/INTAKE.md). **From tickets to a merged spec** - `discovery:create` and `discovery:approve` turn rough input into tickets you approve before they reach the tracker. See [Discovery](docs/WORKFLOW_COMMANDS.md#discovery). - `spec:triage` groups tickets into specs. `spec:create` checks each ticket's readiness against the code, then writes the plan and goal prompt. Specs sit under `docs/specs/{todo,completed}/` with a generated `INDEX.md`. See [Specs](docs/WORKFLOW_COMMANDS.md#specs). - `ticket:execute` and `ticket:complete` build one ticket test first and commit it with a `Ticket: ` trailer. Neither writes to the tracker. See [Tickets](docs/WORKFLOW_COMMANDS.md#tickets). - `spec:review` runs a reviewer panel over the spec diff and a blind verifier per finding, then a rollup and gate. `spec:complete` opens and merges the PR, closes the tickets, and its `docs:verify` step checks the README and `docs/` for claims the diff made stale, fixing each one only on your yes. `spec:status` shows where every spec stands. See [Review and completion](docs/WORKFLOW_COMMANDS.md#review-and-completion). **Goal runs and the guard** - `spec:create` prints launch commands for a goal run over the whole spec or the next batch. The launch denies pushes, PR and issue writes, API writes and questions to you; a stuck ticket is blocked with `guard block` and the run continues. See [Goal Runs](docs/GOAL_RUNS.md). - The ticket guard ships inside the plugin as `runtime/guard.pyz` and runs through `uv run`. Plugin hooks freeze RED tests, re-run GREEN before a goal run stops and restore ticket context after a compaction. They exit at once unless a ticket is in progress. **Current state and assumptions** - `spec:current` checks `docs/system-description.md` against the code and compiles `docs/current-state.json`. `spec:diff [spec ...]` shows what changes if the given specs land in order, with overlaps and each spec's assumptions. See [Current state and assumptions](docs/WORKFLOW_COMMANDS.md#current-state-and-assumptions). - `common-ground` checks those assumptions against the current state through the `assumption-checker` agent and keeps its ground file in the repo as `docs/COMMON-GROUND.md`. See [Common Ground](docs/COMMON_GROUND.md). **Agents and trackers** - Long or parallel work runs in the plugin's agents: `code-reader`, `doc-writer`, `test-writer`, `security-prober`, `architect`, `reviewer`, `verifier` and `assumption-checker`. Agents never commit. See [Agents](docs/WORKFLOW_COMMANDS.md#agents). - Tracker adapters cover Jira, GitHub Issues, GitHub Projects, Linear and text tickets, plus a GitHub code-host adapter. See [Tracker Setup](docs/TRACKER_SETUP.md). **Upgrading from 0.4.x** - The `project::` names are gone. Commands are now `discovery:*`, `spec:*` and `ticket:*`, and "spec" replaces "epic". - `create-implementation-plan` folds into `spec:create` and `complete-epic` into `spec:complete`. `complete-sprint` and the retrospective phase are removed. - `common-ground` used to keep its file under `~/.claude/common-ground/`. When one exists for the repository, it offers to move those assumptions in. ## Quick Start ```bash /plugin marketplace add jeffallan/claude-skills ``` **Then, install the skills:** ```bash /plugin install fullstack-dev-skills@fullstack-dev-skills ``` For all installation methods and first steps, see the [**Quick Start Guide**](QUICKSTART.md). **Full documentation:** [jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills](https://jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills) ## Skills 71 specialized skills across 12 categories covering languages, backend/frontend frameworks, infrastructure, APIs, testing, DevOps, security, data/ML, and platform specialists. See [**Skills Guide**](SKILLS_GUIDE.md) for the full list, decision trees, and workflow combinations. ## Usage Patterns ### Context-Aware Activation Skills activate automatically based on your request: ```bash # Backend Development "Implement JWT authentication in my NestJS API" → Activates: NestJS Expert → Loads: references/authentication.md # Frontend Development "Build a React component with Server Components" → Activates: React Expert → Loads: references/server-components.md ``` ### Multi-Skill Workflows Complex tasks combine multiple skills: ``` Feature Development: Feature Forge → Architecture Designer → Fullstack Guardian → Test Master → DevOps Engineer Bug Investigation: Debugging Wizard → Framework Expert → Test Master → Code Reviewer Security Hardening: Secure Code Guardian → Security Reviewer → Test Master ``` ## Context Engineering Check the assumptions your specs and Claude make against your system's current state with `/common-ground`. See the [**Common Ground Guide**](docs/COMMON_GROUND.md) for full documentation. ## Project Workflow The 13 workflow commands take a group of tickets from your tracker to a reviewed, merged pull request: `spec:triage` groups tickets into specs, `spec:create` plans one, `ticket:execute` and `ticket:complete` build it test-first (by hand or in an unattended goal run), and `spec:review` and `spec:complete` review it and merge it. Specs live as markdown in your repo; tickets stay in Jira, GitHub Issues, GitHub Projects, Linear or text files. See the [**Workflow Commands Reference**](docs/WORKFLOW_COMMANDS.md). `spec:current` and `spec:diff` show the system as it is and what the outstanding specs would change. For an existing codebase, run the `intake` command first. It documents the code, pins its current behavior in tests and tracks its bugs; see [**Intake**](docs/INTAKE.md). ```mermaid flowchart LR disc["discovery:create
discovery:approve"] -.->|new tickets| triage trk["tickets in
your tracker"] --> triage["spec:triage"] --> create["spec:create"] create --> work["ticket:execute
ticket:complete"] --> done["spec:review
spec:complete"] done -->|merged PR| check["spec:current
spec:diff
common-ground"] check -.->|conflict| create ``` > [!TIP] > **Setup:** the workflow needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and a `.claude/workflow-config.json`, which the first command that needs the tracker offers to create. See [**Tracker Setup**](docs/TRACKER_SETUP.md) and [**Goal Runs**](docs/GOAL_RUNS.md). ## Documentation - [**Quick Start Guide**](QUICKSTART.md) - Installation and first steps - [**Skills Guide**](SKILLS_GUIDE.md) - Skill reference and decision trees - [**Workflow Examples**](https://github.com/jeffallan/claude-skills/blob/main/examples/README.md) - Step-by-step multi-skill walkthroughs - [**Common Ground**](docs/COMMON_GROUND.md) - Context engineering with `/common-ground` - [**Workflow Commands**](docs/WORKFLOW_COMMANDS.md) - Project workflow commands guide - [**Tracker Setup**](docs/TRACKER_SETUP.md) - Configure the workflow for your tracker - [**Intake**](docs/INTAKE.md) - Adopt an existing codebase - [**Goal Runs**](docs/GOAL_RUNS.md) - Unattended goal runs over a spec - [**Atlassian MCP Setup**](docs/ATLASSIAN_MCP_SETUP.md) - Atlassian MCP server setup, for Jira - [**Local Development**](docs/local_skill_development.md) - Local skill development - [**Contributing**](CONTRIBUTING.md) - Contribution guidelines - **plugin/skills/\*/SKILL.md** - Individual skill documentation - **plugin/skills/\*/references/** - Deep-dive reference materials ## Contributing See [**Contributing**](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines on adding skills, writing references, and submitting pull requests. ## Changelog See [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for full version history and release notes. ## License MIT License. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. ## Support - **Issues:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/jeffallan/claude-skills/issues) - **Discussions:** [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/jeffallan/claude-skills/discussions) - **Repository:** [github.com/jeffallan/claude-skills](https://github.com/jeffallan/claude-skills) ## Author Built by [**jeffallan**](https://jeffallan.github.io) [](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeff-smolinski/) **Principal Consultant** at [**Synergetic Solutions**](https://synergetic.solutions) [](https://www.linkedin.com/company/synergetic-holdings) Fullstack engineering, security engineering, compliance, and technical due diligence. ## Community ## Star History --- **Built for Claude Code** | **13 Workflows** | **393 Reference Files** | **71 Skills**

releases.name: v0.5.2
releases.body:
### Changed
- Intake: v0.5.0 kept reproduction detail out of git only for Critical and High security findings in public repos or repos of unknown visibility. Now every security finding, at any severity and in every repo, keeps its reproduction detail in the git-excluded `docs/intake-findings-restricted.md`, and its tests are committed with neutral names

### Fixed
- A Stop hook that can't find uv while a ticket is in progress blocks one stop per ticket, then lets the next stop through. A session can't install uv, so blocking every stop kept an unattended goal run going until Claude Code's continuation cap cut it off. The hook records the block in a flag file beside the ticket marker, keyed to the marker's content, so a new ticket is blocked once again. A stop it lets through shows the uv message and says the guard did not run, so GREEN was not checked. When the flag can't be written, the hook blocks every stop as before. The other hooks are unchanged

---

**Documentation:** https://jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills/

releases.name: v0.5.1
releases.body:
### Fixed
- Guard hooks fail closed when uv can't be found while a ticket is in progress. Each hook ran `uv` from the PATH Claude Code starts with, which can lack the shell profile that adds `~/.local/bin` (Claude Code started from a desktop app or an IDE). The hook then exited 127, which Claude Code treats as non-blocking, so edits to frozen RED tests and a goal run's stop check went through unchecked. The hooks now also look in `~/.local/bin` and `~/.cargo/bin`, and otherwise block with a message naming the cause. Without a ticket in progress nothing changes. Goal Runs explains the message
- CI: the Validate job installs uv, which the plugin tree tests need to run the hooks

---

**Documentation:** https://jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills/

releases.name: v0.5.0
releases.body:
### Added
- Workflow: v0.5.0 workflow commands, `spec:triage` and `spec:review`, plus rewritten `discovery:create`, `discovery:approve`, `spec:create`, `spec:complete`, `ticket:execute` and `ticket:complete`. Specs live as markdown under `docs/specs/{todo,completed}/` with a generated `INDEX.md`; tickets stay in the tracker (#253)
- Workflow: tracker adapters for Jira, GitHub Issues, GitHub Projects, Linear and text tickets, and a GitHub code-host adapter, configured in `.claude/workflow-config.json` with a setup wizard (`references/adapters/`). The wizard recommends a tracker only from what the repo shows (an existing config, a tickets folder, a GitHub remote); a Jira or Linear MCP server connected to the session is offered, never recommended on its own (#62, #119)
- Workflow: the ticket guard (marker, hooks, RED and GREEN evidence, boundary checks, review rollup and gate, spec index, batch runner) ships inside the plugin as `runtime/guard.pyz`, run through `uv run`, which supplies Python 3.11 or later when needed. The guard itself is never fetched from PyPI, and the guard is versioned with the commands that call it. Moved from skill-linter 0.3.7, which keeps only the linter

releases.name: v0.4.22
releases.body:
### Added
- Workflow examples: `examples/` holds three step-by-step walkthroughs that chain skills on one task, a Go REST API from spec to Docker image, a slow Django endpoint debugged in production, and JWT authentication for a Spring Boot API, each giving the prompt, the skill it triggers and a short excerpt. The README links them (#317, closing #98)

### Changed
- Handbook v0.6.3: the handbook-update and notes-check workflows run on the runner labels in the `RUNNER_LABELS` variable (default `ubuntu-latest`) and pass the handbook token through the environment instead of `~/.gitconfig`; the docs site moves to Starlight 0.43.1, Astro 7.4.12 and Prettier 3.10.1 (#333)

### Fixed
- Docs site: the README's Workflow Examples link points at GitHub, since the site doesn't publish `examples/` and its link check failed the build after #317

### Contributors
- @CloudCorpRecords: multi-skill workflow examples (#317)

---

**Documentation:** https://jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills/

releases.name: v0.4.21
releases.body:
### Added
- nuxt-expert: Nuxt 4.6 skill for full-stack Nuxt apps, with references on project structure and upgrades (Nuxt 3 to 4, the Nuxt 5 compatibility flag), data fetching, server routes with `nuxt/server`, rendering (route rules, islands, lazy hydration), security (runtime config secrets, nuxt-auth-utils, nuxt-security), deployment and testing. vue-expert's Nuxt 3 reference becomes `references/ssr.md`, limited to Vue SSR without Nuxt, and vue-expert and nextjs-developer link to the new skill (closing #316)
- firebase-expert: Firebase skill for the modular JS SDK 13, firebase-admin 14 and Cloud Functions 2nd gen, with references on Firestore, Security Rules and their emulator tests, Authentication and Identity Platform, Cloud Functions, Storage with App Check and AI Logic, the Emulator Suite, and Hosting and App Hosting deploys. cloud-architect, secure-code-guardian, nextjs-developer, react-expert, flutter-expert and react-native-expert link to it (closing #217)
- flask-expert: Flask 3.1 and SQLAlchemy 2 skill for JSON APIs and server-rendered apps, with references on app structure, the database layer, REST APIs, templates and forms, authentication, testing and deployment. dja

What's New in v0.5.0

v0.5.0 rebuilds the project workflow around specs. Tickets stay in your tracker, specs live as Markdown in your repo, and each ticket is built with its failing test first, by hand or in an unattended goal run.

Install

  • The plugin now ships from the plugin/ folder on main, listed by the root marketplace entry. The Quick Start commands are unchanged. Updating the plugin installs what main holds, and the separate plugin distribution branch is gone. See plugin/README.md.
  • The workflow commands need uv and a .claude/workflow-config.json, which a setup wizard offers to create. See Tracker Setup.

Adopting an existing codebase

  • intake documents the code, pins its current behavior in characterization tests and records each bug it finds as an F-NNN finding while leaving the behavior unchanged. It also writes a baseline spec and docs/system-description.md, and runs by hand or as one goal with a commit per item. See Intake.

From tickets to a merged spec

  • discovery:create and discovery:approve turn rough input into tickets you approve before they reach the tracker. See Discovery.
  • spec:triage groups tickets into specs. spec:create checks each ticket's readiness against the code, then writes the plan and goal prompt. Specs sit under docs/specs/{todo,completed}/ with a generated INDEX.md. See Specs.
  • ticket:execute and ticket:complete build one ticket test first and commit it with a Ticket: <id> trailer. Neither writes to the tracker. See Tickets.
  • spec:review runs a reviewer panel over the spec diff and a blind verifier per finding, then a rollup and gate. spec:complete opens and merges the PR, closes the tickets, and its docs:verify step checks the README and docs/ for claims the diff made stale, fixing each one only on your yes. spec:status shows where every spec stands. See Review and completion.

Goal runs and the guard

  • spec:create prints launch commands for a goal run over the whole spec or the next batch. The launch denies pushes, PR and issue writes, API writes and questions to you; a stuck ticket is blocked with guard block and the run continues. See Goal Runs.
  • The ticket guard ships inside the plugin as runtime/guard.pyz and runs through uv run. Plugin hooks freeze RED tests, re-run GREEN before a goal run stops and restore ticket context after a compaction. They exit at once unless a ticket is in progress.

Current state and assumptions

  • spec:current checks docs/system-description.md against the code and compiles docs/current-state.json. spec:diff [spec ...] shows what changes if the given specs land in order, with overlaps and each spec's assumptions. See Current state and assumptions.
  • common-ground checks those assumptions against the current state through the assumption-checker agent and keeps its ground file in the repo as docs/COMMON-GROUND.md. See Common Ground.

Agents and trackers

  • Long or parallel work runs in the plugin's agents: code-reader, doc-writer, test-writer, security-prober, architect, reviewer, verifier and assumption-checker. Agents never commit. See Agents.
  • Tracker adapters cover Jira, GitHub Issues, GitHub Projects, Linear and text tickets, plus a GitHub code-host adapter. See Tracker Setup.

Upgrading from 0.4.x

  • The project:<phase>:<command> names are gone. Commands are now discovery:*, spec:* and ticket:*, and "spec" replaces "epic".
  • create-implementation-plan folds into spec:create and complete-epic into spec:complete. complete-sprint and the retrospective phase are removed.
  • common-ground used to keep its file under ~/.claude/common-ground/. When one exists for the repository, it offers to move those assumptions in.

Quick Start

/plugin marketplace add jeffallan/claude-skills

Then, install the skills:

/plugin install fullstack-dev-skills@fullstack-dev-skills

For all installation methods and first steps, see the Quick Start Guide.

Full documentation: jeffallan.github.io/claude-skills

Skills

71 specialized skills across 12 categories covering languages, backend/frontend frameworks, infrastructure, APIs, testing, DevOps, security, data/ML, and platform specialists.

See Skills Guide for the full list, decision trees, and workflow combinations.

Usage Patterns

Context-Aware Activation

Skills activate automatically based on your request:

# Backend Development
"Implement JWT authentication in my NestJS API"
→ Activates: NestJS Expert → Loads: references/authentication.md

# Frontend Development
"Build a React component with Server Components"
→ Activates: React Expert → Loads: references/server-components.md

Multi-Skill Workflows

Complex tasks combine multiple skills:

Feature Development: Feature Forge → Architecture Designer → Fullstack Guardian → Test Master → DevOps Engineer
Bug Investigation:   Debugging Wizard → Framework Expert → Test Master → Code Reviewer
Security Hardening:  Secure Code Guardian → Security Reviewer → Test Master

Context Engineering

Check the assumptions your specs and Claude make against your system's current state with /common-ground. See the Common Ground Guide for full documentation.

Project Workflow

The 13 workflow commands take a group of tickets from your tracker to a reviewed, merged pull request: spec:triage groups tickets into specs, spec:create plans one, ticket:execute and ticket:complete build it test-first (by hand or in an unattended goal run), and spec:review and spec:complete review it and merge it. Specs live as markdown in your repo; tickets stay in Jira, GitHub Issues, GitHub Projects, Linear or text files. See the Workflow Commands Reference. spec:current and spec:diff show the system as it is and what the outstanding specs would change. For an existing codebase, run the intake command first. It documents the code, pins its current behavior in tests and tracks its bugs; see Intake.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Collection of 66 specialized skills and workflows for Claude Code.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository provides a comprehensive, curated suite of 66 specialized skills and 9 detailed workflows specifically designed to enhance Claude Code for full-stack developers. It transforms the AI agent into a highly expert pair programmer by providing it with specific, optimized tools for various modern development tasks. The skills cover everything from front-end framework scaffolding to backend database migrations, allowing the agent to perform complex, multi-step coding operations natively. It significantly expands the out-of-the-box capabilities of Claude Code by giving it structured, domain-specific knowledge.
keyFeatures: Extensive skill library: Provides 66 distinct, highly specialized skills targeting various aspects of modern full-stack development.
Curated workflows: Includes 9 structured workflows to guide the AI agent step-by-step through complex, multi-phase tasks.
Seamless integration: Designed to function flawlessly as a drop-in plugin for the existing Claude Code ecosystem.
Standardized formatting: Utilizes standardized formats and structures to ensure predictable and reliable AI behavior during execution.
Continuous expansion: Receives regular updates and additions to support new frameworks, languages, and developer tools.

useCases.title: Full-Stack Scaffolding
useCases.description: Using specialized workflows to rapidly initialize, configure, and structure complex modern web applications.

useCases.title: Targeted Code Refactoring
useCases.description: Applying specific framework skills to intelligently refactor legacy code according to modern best practices.

useCases.title: Automated Testing Setup
useCases.description: Leveraging AI skills to automatically generate and configure comprehensive test suites for newly implemented features.

useCases.title: Database Schema Migration
useCases.description: Assisting developers in designing, generating, and applying complex database migrations using structured agent workflows.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Full-stack developers and software engineers actively using Claude Code who want to significantly extend its technical capabilities. Basic familiarity with Claude Code plugin integration is necessary.
